mainTopic: A גט or קידושין that excludes certain men: the dispute between רבי אליעזר and the רבנן, its sources, and אביי's follow-up cases
overview: This amud opens at the end of a ברייתא. When a גט leaves out one man, רבי אליעזר lets her marry anyone else, and the חכמים say the גט does not work. In the ברייתא's case, which works through a condition, רבי אליעזר compares it to any ordinary condition. The רבנן answer that this condition holds back part of the גט. For the משנה's 'חוץ' case, רבי אליעזר's reason comes from a פסוק. רבי ינאי, quoting an elder, learns it from 'וְהָיְתָה לְאִישׁ אַחֵר', and רבי יוחנן learns it from 'גְּרוּשָׁה מֵאִישָׁהּ'. The רבנן answer each proof. רבי אבא then asks whether קידושין with an exception works, and concludes that קידושין follows the same rule as a גט according to both opinions. אביי uses this to rule on a case of two brothers who each betrothed the same woman, and to explain when she would be 'the wife of two dead men.' Finally, אביי asks what happens when a husband excludes two men in a גט and then says 'to ראובן and שמעון'. That question continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The dispute: free for everyone except one man
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends by stating the dispute. רבי אליעזר permits her to marry anyone except the man who was left out, and the חכמים forbid her to remarry.
steps.simpleTranslation: In this case רבי אליעזר permits her to marry any man except that one man, and the חכמים forbid her.
steps.whatsHappening: We are hearing the closing words of a ברייתא that sets out the basic מחלוקת between רבי אליעזר and the חכמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this case the husband's condition is about one specific man. רבי אליעזר says the גט works, so she may marry everyone except him. The חכמים say the גט does not work at all, so she may not remarry anyone.

keyTerms.meaning: permits (here: says the divorce works and she may remarry)
forbid (here: say the divorce does not work)

phrases.english: that Rabbi Eliezer permits
her to marry any man except for that man,
and the Rabbis forbid.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר מַתִּיר לְכׇל אָדָם חוּץ מֵאוֹתוֹ הָאִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the ברייתא that the earlier discussion on the daf was quoting.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אליעזר: the גט works and she may marry anyone except the one man. חכמים: the גט is not valid.

steps.title: Asking for רבי אליעזר's reason in the ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי אליעזר holds that this גט works.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is רבי אליעזר's reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question that sets up the next step. It wants to know why רבי אליעזר holds that this divorce works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גט is supposed to free the woman completely. Here she stays forbidden to one man, so it is not obvious why רבי אליעזר accepts it.

phrases.english: What is the reason of Rabbi Eliezer?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind the ruling just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רבי אליעזר holds that the גט in the ברייתא works.

steps.title: Just like any ordinary condition
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר's reason is that this case is no different from any other condition a husband attaches to a גט.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is just like all ordinary conditions.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי אליעזר treats this like any normal condition a husband may put on a divorce.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A husband is allowed to give a גט with a condition, and the גט still works. In רבי אליעזר's view, 'on condition that you don't marry so-and-so' is one more condition of that kind.

phrases.english: It is just as it is with all ordinary conditions.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִידֵּי דְּהָוֵה אַכֹּל תְּנָאֵי דְּעָלְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The condition about one man is just like any other condition, so the גט works.

steps.title: The רבנן: this condition holds back part of the גט
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן answer that ordinary conditions leave the גט itself whole. This condition takes away part of her freedom, so the גט is missing something.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן? With all ordinary conditions he did not hold back anything from the גט. Here he did hold back part of the גט.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the רבנן do not accept רבי אליעזר's comparison to ordinary conditions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An ordinary condition only decides whether the גט takes effect. Once it does, she is fully free. A condition about one man leaves her bound to him even after the גט takes effect, so the separation is incomplete and the גט is not valid.
steps.confusionAlert: The רבנן agree that a husband may attach conditions to a גט. They only object to a condition that leaves part of her still bound to him.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis? With all ordinary conditions
he did not leave anything out of the bill of divorce,
phrases.notes: He means the husband did not keep back any piece of her freedom. Once the condition is met, she is fully free.

phrases.english: here he left something out of the bill of divorce for her.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבָּנַן כֹּל תְּנָאֵי דְּעָלְמָא לָא שַׁיַּיר לֵיהּ בְּגֵט
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the רבנן's answer to רבי אליעזר's comparison.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects comparing this condition to ordinary conditions.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Ordinary conditions do not hold back part of the גט. This one does, because she stays forbidden to one man.
steps.whatToRemember: The two sides disagree about whether a condition that bans one man is like any normal condition (רבי אליעזר) or leaves the גט incomplete (רבנן).

steps.title: What is רבי אליעזר's reason in the משנה's 'חוץ' case?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה is about an exception ('except for so-and-so'), not a condition. So the 'ordinary condition' reason does not fit, and the גמרא asks for רבי אליעזר's reason there.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the משנה, which we explained as a case of 'except,' what is רבי אליעזר's reason there?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves back to the משנה and asks a new question. It sets up the next step, which brings a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason from step 3 works only when the husband used a condition. In the משנה's case he wrote 'you are free to all except so-and-so,' which directly limits the גט itself. So רבי אליעזר needs a different reason there.

phrases.english: And our mishna, which we established as dealing with 'except,'
phrases.notes: Earlier on the daf the גמרא explained that the משנה's dispute is about a גט saying 'except for so-and-so,' not about a condition.

phrases.english: what is the reason of Rabbi Eliezer?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַתְנִיתִין דְּאוֹקֵימְנָא בְּחוּץ מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Points out that the reason given in step 3 does not cover the משנה's 'חוץ' case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רבי אליעזר holds that a גט with an exception ('חוץ') works.

steps.title: Learning from 'and becomes another man's wife'
steps.stepSummary: רבי ינאי quotes an elder. The פסוק says 'וְהָיְתָה לְאִישׁ אַחֵר,' so even if the גט frees her only for one other man, she is divorced.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ינאי said in the name of one elder: The פסוק says, 'And she goes out of his house, and goes, and becomes another man's wife.' This teaches that even if he freed her only for another man, she is divorced.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a source from the תורה for רבי אליעזר's view in the 'חוץ' case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The elder reads 'לְאִישׁ אַחֵר' as 'to another man,' meaning even a single one. If a גט that frees her for just one man works, then a גט that frees her for everyone except one man surely works too.
steps.whyThisMatters: This moves רבי אליעזר's view from a reasoning about conditions to a direct reading of the פסוק about divorce.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יַנַּאי מִשּׁוּם זָקֵן אֶחָד,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yannai said in the name of one elder:
The verse says:
'And she goes out of his house, and goes,'
'and becomes another man's wife.'
Even if he did not permit her
except to one other man,
she is divorced.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יַנַּאי מִשּׁוּם זָקֵן אֶחָד אָמַר קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק 'לְאִישׁ אַחֵר' shows that freeing her for even one man makes the divorce work.

steps.title: The רבנן: 'man' means every man
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן answer the elder's proof. In the פסוק, 'אִישׁ' means any and every man, so the גט must free her for everyone.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן say about רבי אליעזר's reason: This word 'man' means every single man.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows how the רבנן read the same פסוק differently and so reject רבי אליעזר's proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides use the same words 'לְאִישׁ אַחֵר.' The רבנן read it as 'free to marry any other man she chooses.' On that reading, a גט that leaves out even one man does not meet the פסוק's requirement.
steps.whatToRemember: The whole dispute in the 'חוץ' case depends on the word 'אִישׁ' in the פסוק. רבי אליעזר reads it as even one man, and the רבנן read it as any man at all.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis say,
regarding the reason of Rabbi Eliezer:
this word 'man' means to each and every man.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבָּנַן אָמְרִי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the רבנן's answer to the proof from the פסוק in step 6.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: 'אִישׁ' means any man, not just one man, so the פסוק requires her to be free to marry anyone.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן's source: the verse about priests
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says רבי אליעזר's source is the פסוק forbidding a כהן to marry 'a woman divorced from her husband.' Even a woman divorced only from her husband counts as divorced, so a גט with one exception is surely a real גט.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: רבי אליעזר's reason comes from this פסוק: 'And a woman divorced from her husband they shall not take.' This means that even if she was divorced only from her husband, and not freed for anyone else, she is already forbidden to a כהן. So we see it counts as a גט.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second, different source for רבי אליעזר's view, in place of the elder's proof quoted by רבי ינאי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'divorced from her husband' suggest a divorce that only separates her from him, without freeing her for anyone else. If even that counts as divorce for the כהונה rule, then a גט that frees her for everyone except one man is surely a real גט.

keyTerms.meaning: She becomes forbidden to marry a כהן

steps.whyThisMatters: This proof rests on a different פסוק and does not depend on how to read the word 'אִישׁ', so the רבנן need a different answer to it (step 9).

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said:
The reason of Rabbi Eliezer is from here:
"And a woman divorced from her husband they shall not take"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 21:7. The פסוק is talking about whom a כהן may not marry.

phrases.english: even if she was divorced only from her husband,
she is disqualified from the priesthood.
Apparently, it is a valid bill of divorce.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר, טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר מֵהָכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, independent answer to the question of step 5. It is a different source for רבי אליעזר than the elder's proof quoted by רבי ינאי in step 6.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is רבי אליעזר's source in the exception case? (from step 5)
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק 'וְאִשָּׁה גְּרוּשָׁה מֵאִישָׁהּ' shows that even a partial divorce counts as divorce.

steps.title: The רבנן: the כהונה rule is a special case
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן answer that the כהונה prohibition is different. It applies even when the divorce is not a fully valid one, so we cannot prove from it that the גט works.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן would say: the prohibition for a כהן is different.
steps.whatsHappening: The רבנן push back on רבי יוחנן's proof by saying the כהונה rule cannot teach us about a real גט.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the כהונה rule, even a weak or incomplete divorce is enough to forbid her to a כהן. That is a stricter rule. It does not show that such a divorce actually frees her from her husband.

keyTerms.meaning: The prohibition of a woman marrying a כהן

steps.confusionAlert: The רבנן agree she cannot marry a כהן. They only deny that this proves the גט frees her to remarry.
steps.whatToRemember: Two sources for רבי אליעזר: the elder's 'וְהָיְתָה לְאִישׁ אַחֵר' and רבי יוחנן's 'גְּרוּשָׁה מֵאִישָׁהּ'. The רבנן answer each one: 'אִישׁ' means every man, and the כהונה rule is a special case.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis?
The prohibition of the priesthood is different.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבָּנַן – אִיסּוּר כְּהוּנָּה שָׁאנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבי יוחנן's proof from step 8.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof. The כהונה law itself stays in place.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The כהונה prohibition is stricter and applies even to a divorce that is not fully valid, so it cannot prove what makes a valid גט.

steps.title: רבי אבא asks: what about קידושין with an exception?
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא asks whether קידושין with an exception works. For example, the man makes her forbidden to everyone except one man. He says the question can be asked according to both רבי אליעזר and the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא asked: in קידושין, how is it? The question can be asked according to רבי אליעזר, and it can be asked according to the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question, moving from גט to קידושין. It announces that the question works for both opinions and is about to explain each side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the topic was a גט with an exception. רבי אבא asks whether the same kind of exception works when a man betroths a woman. He notes the doubt exists no matter whose view on divorce we follow.

keyTerms.meaning: Betrothal, the first stage of marriage
Let the question be asked, it is a question

phrases.english: Rabbi Abba asked:
In betrothal, how is it?
Let it be asked according to Rabbi Eliezer,
let it be asked according to the Rabbis.

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּעֵי רַבִּי אַבָּא: בְּקִידּוּשִׁין הֵיאַךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the topic of a גט with an exception to the parallel case in קידושין.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does קידושין with an exception (forbidden to all but one man) take effect?

steps.title: The two sides of the question for רבי אליעזר
steps.stepSummary: According to רבי אליעזר, maybe he allowed the exception only in a גט, because פסוקים taught it, while קידושין needs a full acquisition. Or maybe the פסוק links leaving one marriage with entering the next, so קידושין follows the same rule as a גט.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let it be asked according to רבי אליעזר: maybe רבי אליעזר said this only here, because פסוקים are written about it, but there, in betrothal, we need a complete acquisition. Or maybe we compare 'and she leaves' to 'and she becomes.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רבי אליעזר's view leaves room for doubt about קידושין. It lays out both possible ways to see it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Side one: the exception worked in a גט only because special פסוקים taught it. Without such a source, קידושין must be a complete קנין, and an exception makes it incomplete. Side two: the פסוק joins 'וְיָצְאָה' (leaving through divorce) with 'וְהָיְתָה' (becoming another man's wife), so whatever works in a גט also works in קידושין.

keyTerms.meaning: He only said it until here, his ruling is limited to this case
'And she leaves... and becomes', the linking of divorce and betrothal

steps.confusionAlert: This is a question, not a ruling. Here both sides are only possibilities. רבי אבא decides the question in step 13.

phrases.english: Let it be asked according to Rabbi Eliezer:

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר הָכָא,
phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer said it only here, by divorce,
because verses are written about it;
phrases.notes: These are the פסוקים from steps 6 and 8.

phrases.english: but there, by betrothal,
we require a complete acquisition.
Or perhaps
"And she leaves" is compared to "and she becomes."
phrases.notes: דברים 24:2. The פסוק puts leaving one marriage right next to entering the next, so they follow the same rules.

steps.triggerLanguage: תִּיבְּעֵי לְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר – עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר הָכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the first half of רבי אבא's question from step 10, the side according to רבי אליעזר.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is רבי אליעזר's acceptance of the exception limited to a גט, or does the היקש of 'וְיָצְאָה' and 'וְהָיְתָה' carry it over to קידושין?

steps.title: The same question according to the רבנן
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא asks his question according to the רבנן. Maybe they reject a גט with an exception only because a גט needs a full cut, while קידושין needs only some acquisition. Or maybe the פסוק links the two, so קידושין with an exception fails too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let the question be asked according to the רבנן. Maybe the רבנן said a גט with an exception fails only because a גט needs a full cutting off, and that is missing. But there, by קידושין, any kind of acquisition is enough. Or maybe the פסוק links 'and she leaves' to 'and she becomes,' so the two follow the same rule.
steps.whatsHappening: Step 11 asked the question according to רבי אליעזר. Now the גמרא asks the same question according to the רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן said a גט with an exception does not work, because a גט must cut the bond completely. One side of the question says קידושין is different: even a partial acquisition might be enough to make her married. The other side says the פסוק ties leaving one marriage to entering the next, so if an exception ruins a גט, it also ruins קידושין.

keyTerms.meaning: Let the question be asked (here: according to a certain opinion)
A full cutting off; a גט must completely end the bond
Any acquisition at all, even a small or partial one
'And she leaves' and 'and she becomes,' two words from the פסוק that tie divorce to the next marriage

steps.confusionAlert: Notice that the question flips direction depending on whose view we use. For רבי אליעזר the doubt is whether קידושין might be stricter than a גט. For the רבנן the doubt is whether קידושין might be easier than a גט.

phrases.english: Let it be asked according to the Rabbis:

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמְרִי רַבָּנַן הָכָא,
phrases.english: The Rabbis only said here that it does not work
because we need a full cutting off, and there is none;
but there, any acquisition at all is enough.
Or perhaps 'and she leaves' is linked to 'and she becomes.'

steps.triggerLanguage: תִּיבְּעֵי לְרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks the same question as Step 11, this time according to the רבנן.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: According to the רבנן, is קידושין with an exception valid because a partial acquisition is enough, or invalid because the פסוק links it to a גט?

steps.title: רבי אבא answers his own question
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא answers his own question. According to both רבי אליעזר and the רבנן, קידושין follows the same rule as a גט because of the link between 'and she leaves' and 'and she becomes.'
steps.simpleTranslation: After he asked the question, he answered it himself. Both according to רבי אליעזר and according to the רבנן, we use the link between 'and she leaves' and 'and she becomes.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא answers the question he just asked. קידושין and גט follow the same rule according to both opinions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The link in the פסוק decides the question. So for רבי אליעזר, קידושין with an exception works, just as a גט with an exception works. For the רבנן, קידושין with an exception fails, just as a גט with an exception fails, so the same argument carries over to קידושין.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked it as a question
Both this one and that one

steps.whatToRemember: The rule for קידושין mirrors the rule for a גט. Whatever each opinion holds about a גט with an exception, it holds the same about קידושין with an exception.
steps.whyThisMatters: This answer sets up אביי's next statement, which assumes that for רבי אליעזר, קידושין with an exception really works.

phrases.english: After he asked it as a question,
he then answered it himself:
both according to Rabbi Eliezer and according to the Rabbis,
we need the link between 'and she leaves' and 'and she becomes.'

steps.triggerLanguage: לְבָתַר דְּאִיבַּעְיָא לֵיהּ, הֲדַר פַּשְׁטַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the question raised in Steps 10–12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: According to both opinions, קידושין is compared to a גט through the link between 'וְיָצְאָה' and 'וְהָיְתָה,' so the disagreement about a גט applies to קידושין too.

steps.title: אביי's case of two brothers who each married her with an exception
steps.stepSummary: אביי builds on רבי אבא's answer. ראובן married a woman except for שמעון, and שמעון married her except for ראובן. Both died. אביי rules that she may do יבום with לוי, and she is not counted as 'the wife of two dead men.'
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: If you say that רבי אבא's answer is correct, then consider this case. ראובן came and married her, leaving out שמעון. Then שמעון came and married her, leaving out ראובן. Both of them died. She may do יבום with לוי, and I do not call her 'the wife of two dead men.'
steps.whatsHappening: אביי says that if we accept רבי אבא's answer that קידושין with an exception works for רבי אליעזר, a ruling about יבום follows from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ראובן left out שמעון, so she was still free for שמעון when he came to betroth her. Normally, a woman tied to a brother through two dead husbands cannot do יבום. אביי rules that this woman is not counted as 'the wife of two dead men,' so לוי may do יבום with her. The next step explains why.

keyTerms.meaning: If you will say; 'if we accept that...'
She does יבום (marries the dead husband's brother)
The wife of two dead men; a woman who cannot do יבום because she is tied to the brother through two dead husbands

steps.confusionAlert: ראובן, שמעון and לוי are three brothers. That is why the case is about יבום, which is the מצוה for a brother of the dead husband.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
If you will say
that Rabbi Abba's answer is correct,
then if Reuven came and married her except for Shimon,
and Shimon came and married her except for Reuven,
and both of them died,
she does yibum with Levi,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין אֲנִי קוֹרֵא בָּהּ ״אֵשֶׁת שְׁנֵי מֵתִים״.
phrases.english: and I do not call her 'the wife of two dead men.'
phrases.notes: Usually a woman tied to the brother through two dead husbands cannot do יבום. אביי says this rule does not apply here.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: אִם תִּמְצָא לוֹמַר אִיתָא לִדְרַבִּי אַבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds a new יבום ruling on top of רבי אבא's answer in Step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If קידושין with an exception works, a woman married by ראובן except for שמעון, and then by שמעון except for ראובן, may do יבום with לוי after both die. She is not considered 'the wife of two dead men.'

steps.title: Why she is not the wife of two dead men
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains אביי's ruling. ראובן's קידושין worked, but שמעון's קידושין did nothing, so she counts as the wife of only one man.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? ראובן's betrothal worked, and שמעון's betrothal did not work.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the reason behind אביי's ruling that the woman may do יבום with לוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ראובן's קידושין already forbade her to everyone except שמעון. When שמעון betrothed her except for ראובן, he tried to forbid her to people who were already forbidden. So his קידושין added nothing, and she is really only ראובן's wife.

keyTerms.meaning: They did not work, they had no effect

phrases.english: What is the reason?
Reuven's betrothal worked,
Shimon's betrothal did not work.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא? קִידּוּשֵׁי דִרְאוּבֵן אַהֲנוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason for אביי's ruling in step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In אביי's case only ראובן's קידושין took effect, because שמעון's added no new restriction.

steps.title: So when would she be the wife of two dead men?
steps.stepSummary: If אביי's case is not 'the wife of two dead men,' the גמרא asks what case would be.
steps.simpleTranslation: But then, how do you find a case of 'the wife of two dead men'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a case where both brothers' קידושין really take effect. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After saying that אביי's case does not count, the גמרא wants to show that the idea of 'the wife of two dead men' can still happen with קידושין that have an exception. Seeing such a case makes clear what was missing in אביי's case.

keyTerms.meaning: The wife of two dead men, a woman tied to two dead brothers, who cannot do יבום with the surviving brother
How do you find it? In what case does this happen?

phrases.english: But then, the wife of two dead men
how do you find it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֶלָּא אֵשֶׁת שְׁנֵי מֵתִים הֵיכִי מַשְׁכַּחַתְּ לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Since step 15 said אביי's case does not count, the גמרא asks what case does.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A case where both brothers' קידושין take effect, making her 'the wife of two dead men.'

steps.title: A case where both betrothals take effect
steps.stepSummary: ראובן betroths her except for שמעון, and then שמעון betroths her with no exception. Both קידושין work, so she is the wife of two dead men.
steps.simpleTranslation: For example, ראובן betrothed her except for שמעון, and שמעון then betrothed her with no conditions. ראובן's betrothal forbade her to the whole world, and שמעון's betrothal forbade her to ראובן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question with a case where each brother's קידושין adds a real restriction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ראובן's קידושין forbids her to everyone except שמעון. שמעון's plain קידושין forbids her to everyone, which now includes ראובן, so it adds something new. Since both took effect, if both die she cannot do יבום with לוי.

keyTerms.meaning: Plainly, with no conditions or exceptions
To the whole world, to everyone

steps.whatToRemember: קידושין only 'work' if they add a new restriction. In אביי's case שמעון's added nothing. In this case שמעון's plain קידושין forbade her to ראובן, so both count.

phrases.english: For example, where Reuven came
and betrothed her except for Shimon,
and Shimon came and betrothed her plainly,
since Reuven's betrothal worked
to forbid her to the whole world,
phrases.notes: Everyone except שמעון, the one he left out.

phrases.english: and Shimon's betrothal worked
to forbid her to Reuven.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּגוֹן שֶׁבָּא רְאוּבֵן וְקִידְּשָׁהּ חוּץ מִשִּׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: When ראובן betroths her except for שמעון and שמעון betroths her plainly, both קידושין take effect and she is the wife of two dead men.

steps.title: אביי asks about a גט where the exception is changed
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks: a husband gives a גט saying she is permitted to everyone except ראובן and שמעון, and then says 'to ראובן and שמעון.' What is the law?
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי asked: if a husband said to her, 'You are permitted to any man except ראובן and שמעון,' and then said, 'to ראובן and שמעון,' what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי opens a new question about a גט where the husband first makes an exception and then adds a second statement about those same men.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We already learned that a גט with an exception is a problem according to the רבנן. Here the husband seems to fix the exception, but his second words are unclear. אביי asks what those words do.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked, raised a question (a dilemma)
Permitted to any man, the key words of a גט

phrases.english: Abaye asked:
if he said to her
"You are hereby permitted to any man,
except for Reuven and Shimon,"
and then he said to her again:
"to Reuven and Shimon," what is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּעֵי אַבָּיֵי, אָמַר לָהּ: הֲרֵי אַתְּ מוּתֶּרֶת לְכׇל אָדָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from קידושין with an exception to a new question about a גט whose exception is later changed.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What a husband's second statement, 'to ראובן and שמעון,' does to a גט that excluded them.

steps.title: Two ways to understand the husband's second words
steps.stepSummary: Did the husband only permit ראובן and שמעון, so she is now allowed to everyone? Or did he flip it, permitting only ראובן and שמעון and forbidding everyone else?
steps.simpleTranslation: Do we say: what he forbade, he now permitted? Or perhaps: what he forbade, he now permitted, and what he permitted, he now forbade?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out the two sides of אביי's question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Side one: 'to ראובן and שמעון' just adds them, so she is permitted to everyone and the גט is complete. Side two: the new words replace the old ones, so she is permitted only to ראובן and שמעון and forbidden to everyone else, which leaves a large exception.
steps.confusionAlert: The words 'what he forbade, he permitted' appear in both sides. The difference is only the added words 'and what he permitted, he forbade' in the second side.

phrases.english: Do we say:
what he forbade, he permitted;
phrases.notes: So now ראובן and שמעון are allowed too, and she may marry anyone.

phrases.english: or perhaps:
what he forbade, he permitted,
and what he permitted, he forbade?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי אָמְרִינַן: מַאי דַּאֲסַר שְׁרָא; אוֹ דִלְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the two possible answers to אביי's question in step 18.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the second statement only adds ראובן and שמעון, or replaces the first statement entirely.

steps.title: Opening the next layer of the question
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins 'If you say,' getting ready to ask a follow-up question that depends on one side of the first question.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say...
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא is starting a follow-up: even if we decide one way on the first question, a new question will come up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'אם תמצא לומר' builds a chain of questions. It assumes one answer to the first question for the sake of argument and then asks something further. The rest of the question continues on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say, assuming one answer in order to ask a further question

phrases.english: If you say

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם תִּמְצָא לוֹמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a follow-up question that builds on the two sides laid out in step 19.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A further question that depends on how the first question is answered. It continues on the next amud.
